notes: `upstream` is the Isol8 PAPERCLIP FORK image (ghcr.io/isol8ai/paperclip, built by the fork's own CI from branch isol8/2026.8-circuit-breaker, tag v2026.8-isol8.6), pinned by DIGEST. v2026.8-isol8.6 carries ONE change on top of .5: the `hmac_sha1` webhook trigger signing mode (#18) — the SHA-1 twin of github_hmac (HMAC-SHA1 hex over the raw body, optional sha1= prefix, read from X-Paperclip-Signature or a hub-style header), for providers that still sign with SHA-1 (Vercel's x-vercel-signature, Intercom's X-Hub-Signature). A named mode, so no schema change; assertAgentCannotWeakenWebhookAuth ranks it with the SHA-256 modes (HMAC collision-irrelevance). v2026.8-isol8.5 carried TWO changes on top of .3. (a) ISSUE-PREFIX RE-DERIVATION ON RENAME (#16): a company's issue prefix is derived from its name at INSERT, but Isol8 creates the company under a placeholder (a personal owner's email local part) and the CEO agent renames it minutes later during its first run — so every board's task keys froze as three letters of the placeholder (`PRA-1` for prasiddha@…). `update()` now re-derives the prefix when the name changes AND the board has minted no identifiers (issueCounter 0, no cases); once anything is minted the prefix is permanent, so an established board can never be re-keyed. Allocation for BOTH create and rename runs through one `allocateIssuePrefix` holding a per-base transaction-scoped advisory lock (`pg_advisory_xact_lock`, the idiom nextCaseIdentity already uses) — without it concurrent allocators each pre-select the same free candidate and all but one lose the unique index. Every identifier mint (issue create, bulk import, nextCaseIdentity) reads the prefix under `FOR UPDATE` on the company row so it cannot mint from a prefix a rename is replacing. Conflict retries WRAP the transaction, never sit inside it: Postgres aborts a transaction on 23505, so an in-place retry fails 25P02 — reachable because `resolveCloudTenantActor` (middleware/auth.ts) inserts a company with its own stack-derived prefix without taking the lock. (b) WEBHOOK TRIGGERS WITH CALLER-SUPPLIED SECRETS (#17, separately tagged v2026.8-isol8.4, which was superseded by this tag rather than pinned on its own). v2026.8-isol8.3 added exactly one thing: `issue.thread_interaction_created` on the plugin event bus, so the bundled isol8.notifications forwarder can see the event that parks an issue on a human. Before it, eventTypeForActivityAction resolved that action through PLUGIN_EVENT_TYPES, found nothing, returned null, and persistActivity built no pluginEvent at all — there was no subscription any plugin could write for it. Prod had logged 27 of these (four EXPIRED unanswered) and zero approvals, so the one family that actually stops work was the one family nothing could hear. Purely additive to the enum; no other subscriber changes behaviour. v2026.8-isol8.2 REBASED the whole patch stack onto upstream master f554d6737 (2026-08-05). The branch was renamed from isol8/2026.7-circuit-breaker, which is deliberately left unmoved at c9d68063 as the pre-rebase rollback ref. What the rebase brings: DEFAULT-OPEN VISIBLE ISSUE WRITES (upstream #10804) — an agent that can read a company-visible issue may now comment on it, update its fields, create children, and assign it, replacing the narrow ownership/mention grants that previously denied every cross-agent write. Before this, `issue:mutate` had no permission-key mapping and no manager clause, so decideBase fell through to deny_unsupported_action, and the CEO/manager `tasks:manage_active_checkouts` override in assertAgentIssueMutationAllowed was UNREACHABLE (the coarse boundary check runs first) — that is why Friday, seeded role="ceo", got a 403 trying to close a Jarvis-owned task. The assignee run-lock while an issue is `in_progress` survives, and the checkout override now sits above it. Also in: governed interaction addressees (migrations 0203/0204), cross-task write attribution + audit receipts + actionable denials (#10843), contained cross-issue side effects (#10837), the maintained in_review review-path contract (#10675), heartbeat shared-workspace serialization, and the decisions/queues feature (0197-0202). Rebase surgeries to know about: our routine-circuit-breaker migration was renumbered 0197 -> 0209 (upstream now owns 0197-0208) with the journal `when` held at 1784300000000 so already-migrated DBs skip it — re-verified against drizzle-orm 0.45.2's migrator, which reads max(created_at) ONCE before the loop and applies an entry only when that value is below its folderMillis, so our low `when` is skipped on dev/prod (whose max is upstream 0196's 1785170001001) while a fresh DB still gets it in journal order; the SQL is IF NOT EXISTS as a second guard. COMPANY_DELETE_SEQUENCE was extended to cover the eleven new decisions/secret-proposal tables, which hold NO ACTION references to companies/agents/issues/heartbeat_runs/agent_api_keys and would otherwise 500 DELETE /api/companies/:id again (decision_effect_executions is deliberately excluded: no company_id, emptied by cascade from decisions). The fork's docker.yml also needed a lowercase step for upstream's new registry-backed BuildKit cache — buildx rejects the capitals in `Isol8AI/paperclip`. NEW fork patches carried forward from isol8.8: accepted-interaction requeue backoff and the productivity-review stale sweep. Carried patches, all still real source on the fork: the routine circuit breaker, the agent-delete routines-FK fix, honest run-log workspace/session-reset lines for cloud-adapter runs, the 400 guard on non-UUID X-Paperclip-Run-Id headers, complete child-row cleanup on issue delete, the agent-comment whitespace fix, the resilient detached agent.wait (<=5-min slices across the API Gateway 2h WS cap, 48h ceiling), the FK-safe company delete (COMPANY_DELETE_SEQUENCE), daily-cap retry parking, the PAPERCLIP_SKIP_BUILTIN_AGENTS gate (Isol8 tenants get exactly Friday+Atlas; wired in paperclip-stack.ts), and the bundled isol8.notifications forwarder (issue.thread_interaction_created + approval.created/resubmitted + agent.run.finished/failed -> backend /webhooks/paperclip-events; unconfigured instances no-op). The extended Dockerfile is a thin passthrough that re-tags this image into ECR so per-tenant ECS tasks can pull it with execution-role creds (the fork GHCR package is private; the build authenticates with GITHUB_TOKEN and the package grants Isol8AI/isol8 read access). `extendedImage` + per-env `dev.tag`/`prod.tag` are the ECR-published extended image deployed to dev/prod — merging a digest bump here builds the extended image, and its tag is then bumped into `dev.tag` (validate) and `prod.tag` (promote) in follow-up PRs. `upstreamCommit` is the FORK commit (drives the extended tag). Bump `upstream` here to the fork's new digest when shipping fork changes.
